name: Quahuacan Cliff
desc: Living with the Qucusaurs, this is the home of the tribe known as the Flower-Feather Clan. Every day, members of the tribe fly with the Qucusaurs, patrolling their territory from the air.

desc.text:
"This is the tribal affairs noticeboard. Important matters will be discussed here, and you can also leave a message here if you have any questions."
"Urgent matters can be brought to a flying squad or Chief Mutota directly."

"The Floating Target Balloons training module is now open to the public. Come one, come all, and come improve your shooting skills any time."
"There is no barrier to entry for this project. Any warrior wishing to hone themselves can experience the same level of elite training as the flying squads do."
"Note from Chief Mutota: Out of an abundance of caution, this project will be temporarily closed while adverse weather conditions prevail. We seek the understanding of all potential challengers in this."

<color=#ffffffa6>(After completing the Tribal Chronicles "Of Fading Flowers and Falling Feathers")</color>
"The phlogiston-engineered flight device poses a major safety risk at present, and its personal use has been temporarily restricted."
"If it is needed, please report to Chief Mutota first. This rule applies to flying squads as a whole."

"Warriors of the Flower-Feather Clan! The battle horns have been sounded, and the time to seize your glory has arrived! The Pilgrimage of the Return of the Sacred Flame is about to begin!"
"The Peacemaker, Chasca, makes her highly-anticipated return. May she be a role model to you all, to strive past your limits and win ultimate glory amidst challenges!"
"Remember always that there are no chains in all the world that could hope to shackle the Flower-Feather Clan, no limits that her descendants shall not smash through!"

<color=#ffffffa6>(After completing the Archon Quest Chapter V: Act V "Incandescent Ode of Resurrection")</color>
"Warriors of the Flower-Feather Clan, thank you for all that you have given, and all that you have sacrificed. It is through your deeds that victory was won."
"From the day of this announcement, the Flower-Feather Clan is no longer in a state of war. The peacetime rules of the Flight Trial are hereby reinstated."
"Members of the flying squad should change shifts according to the new patrol and training plans."
"The Abyss may have been defeated, but other dangers may rise in its wake. Remain vigilant, and never forget your pride as warriors. Always remember to hone your skills."

"50 million Mora and several years of construction work later, the all-new shooting range, The Flowerbed, will open in three days. Welcome one, welcome all!"
"Entrance is a one-off payment of just 7,000 Mora for lifetime access! Come in and test your limits!"
<color=#37ffff>Message</color> : "Isn't 7,000 Mora a little steep? It's just a shooting range, and it doesn't look like it's offering anything new..."
<color=#37ffff>Another Person's Message</color> : "No, no, no, just think about it. Building everything cost so much Mora and took so long. If it weren't worth it, don't you think work would've been halted long ago?"
<color=#37ffff>Message</color> : "You have a point. In any case, it's lifetime access, so..."

"Due to training not achieving the desired effects, this shooting range will hereby be permanently closed from today onward. Its reopening will be announced at a separate date."
"Admission fees have been refunded. We thank you for your support, and seek your kind understanding in this decision."
<color=#37ffff>Message</color> : "It's nice that we can get our Mora back... But it hasn't even been a fortnight yet, has it?"

<color=#ffffffa6>(After completing the Archon Quest Chapter V: Act V "Incandescent Ode of Resurrection")</color>
"Children of Tlalocan, hear my voice."
"Remember how helpless the people were, when the sky darkened and the Sacred Flame was snuffed out."
"Victory is a warrior's mark of honor, excellence is a hero's chosen path."
"Verses sang in unison give strength to
— they let the voices of Natlan pierce the darkness of the night..."
"This is the flight trial grounds. All personnel must obey regulations to avoid unnecessary accidents."

"8. In non-emergency situations, please follow the ground guides, keep to fixed flight paths, and take off and landings at safe speeds. Dangerous actions are strictly prohibited."
"Note: 'The Saurian did it' shall not be considered an acceptable excuse. Qucusaurs have an innate capacity for safe flight, but humans do not."

"26: Please do not carry any valuables with you when flying to avoid dropping them."
"If a similar situation occurs, please ask any flying squad for assistance."
<color=#37ffff>Chief's Message</color> : "Due to the variance in difficulty involved in finding different items, our flying squads cannot guarantee definite retrieval of any lost belongings. Please pay close attention and follow all regulations."

"34: Those who release junk while airborne will be subject to lifetime imprisonment."
"For the safety of everyone, nobody is allowed to release any airborne objects around the trial grounds without obtaining prior approval. This includes kites, balloons, and birds!"
"In a previous case, someone released a balloon and it impacted a Qucusaurus' flight path. If it weren't for a flying squad member administering timely assistance, the results would have been disastrous!"
"The chief has also stated that safety is paramount. This kind of thing cannot happen again. So follow the rules, everyone!"

"37: For safety reasons, please do not carry any creatures with you incapable of flight."
"Note: In theory, humans are also a species without plumage who walk on two legs, and who are incapable of flight."
"Further Note: 'My friend has a wind glider — that totally counts as having flight capabilities' shall not be considered a valid excuse."

"52: Do not shout or scream while flying, and do not make strange noises."
"The former will disorient other people (or Saurians), while the latter may be misinterpreted as an instruction by Qucusaurs, thus creating unnecessary safety hazards."
"Note: 'I'm singing' shall not be considered a valid excuse for making strange noises. The definition of what constitutes a 'song' here shall be left to the majority consensus of people (or Saurians)."

"All candidates wishing to take part in the flight test must first clear mental aptitude and physical examinations before being allowed to practice take-offs."
"Meanwhile, all flight-related training must be conducted under the protection and supervision of a tutor. Any unauthorized training will result in permanent loss of eligibility for flight trials."
"Administrators reserve the right to terminate any training currently underway, and if a termination signal is received, please follow all instructions in returning to the arena."

"Listen carefully, everyone: I have discussed this with the chief, and everyone needs to be examined again. Only those who make the cut in both mental and physical aptitude will be issued their wings once more!"
"Otherwise, you will be required to stay in the vicinity of the arena to receive treatment. All candidates must undergo re-examination, especially anyone who has come into contact with Abyssal forces!"
"Of course, if you don't wish to undergo testing again, all you have to do is beat Miss Chasca in combat, and we'll consider you fighting fit!"
"Can't quite manage that? Haha, then quit yapping and get your treatment sorted! Once treated, you'll be allowed to fly again."

<color=#ffffffa6>(Before completing the Archon Quest Chapter V: Act IV "The Rainbow Destined to Burn")</color>
"I hope you all remember to perform regular health checkups on yourself and your Saurian companions. Like humans, they can be quite obstinate at times."
"If you feel as though something is off during your daily interactions with them, please come in for a check-up immediately. Doctor Chuychu and I can both help out."
"I recommend Doctor Chuychu for human injuries. If a Saurian is injured, come find me."
"Anyway, don't be pig-headed. This applies to both humans and Saurians."

<color=#ffffffa6>(After completing the Archon Quest Chapter V: Act IV "The Rainbow Destined to Burn")</color>
"I hope you all remember to perform regular health checkups on your Saurian companions. Like humans, they can be quite obstinate at times."
"If you feel as though something is off during your daily interactions with them, please come in for a check-up immediately. I will do my best to help in my capacity as a doctor, whether it be for you or your companion."
"Anyway, don't be pig-headed, alright? This applies to both humans and Saurians."

(Childish, scribbled writings are visible:)
This game's called "Bing Bong Ding Dong," and here's the rules:
1. When the Bing Bong Monetoo isn't ding-donging, ride on the Saurian statue's back to make it move forward.
2. Get off the Saurian statue when the Bing Bong Monetoo counts down to a "ding!" or you'll lose.
3. First one to run to the Bing Bong Monetoo wins!
And don't give me that "isn't this just Red Light, Green Light?" crap. Rules are important, and it's precisely because you don't respect the rules that you can't win!
(A work by Fontainian playwright, Jean Brooklyn. A book this thick can totally be used by shorter people to increase their height.)
(The biography of Frank Drebin, retired Inspector of Fontaine's Marechaussee Phantom special police force. Yep, the Inspector is a vigorous white cat.)
(A romance novel written by Dorothy Leeckson. On its faded cover, a woman lies on a bed surrounded by flowers.)

"Creating murals in places where paint is produced is indeed a good idea. When we repair them, we can <color=#37ffff>just grab the relevant material on the spot and fill the missing paints in</color> ..."
"...The story couldn't possibly end just as the three tribal warriors were defeated by Rumi the wicked sorcerer. Could the mural in which Kuntur appears be somewhere else?..."
"...I can't find the path. Has it been buried? Or is there some sort of mechanism at play here..."
"...Alright. Now then, you're coming with me, and we're going to track down Rumi the sorcerer — for my honor... Uh, and also for the warriors who were turned into Pakpakas..."

...
Aj Awaj K'umilal Kan stormed into my laboratory in a fit of rage. He interrogated me, demanding to know if I had taught the humans how to use phlogiston. I assuaged his fury with Quenepa Berries and asked what had happened.
According to his account, it seems that a human colony near Q'umqaraq'aj has mastered the power of phlogiston and begun to expand. In the last three months, they've razed over (...) villages, sacrificed roughly (...) human victims, and clogged the River Tz'alam's very flow with discarded (...). Their leader claims to be the "Successor of Chaac," swearing to end the age of dragons and to unite the people of Natlantea under a single banner. Ix Roq'ratik'obala' Ka'alahun quelled the uprising in two days. The would-be conqueror was drowned in his own bath by his most favored consort, a captive turned killer. Leaderless, the tribe collapsed into internecine strife. Yet the secrets of phlogiston had already spread, now utterly beyond containment.
"Hmph... If you, milord, with your tender heart, have not sanctioned this folly, then the only one mad enough to dare would be..."
Awaj did not finish his sentence, muttering under his breath as he left. Truth be told, he likely concerns himself little about humans mastering phlogiston. His fury stems solely from the crudeness of their methods, a blasphemy against his life's work.
But I care. I cannot comprehend why Kukulkan (for it must be him, after all, no other would do such a foolish thing) would hand phlogiston over to the humans. I can understand his antipathy for these tiny lifeforms, brought by the usurper from beyond the sky, but I cannot comprehend his use of this method to lure them into destroying themselves. It is like handing a rusty knife to a wailing infant — all too vicious, and all too cruel. What outcome could he possibly expect, save for suffering and death?
...
I met with Kukulkan in private and asked him about his intentions.
As usual, he remained enigmatic and aloof. He coldly denied all accusations. He claimed that I was not truly concerned about how this matter harmed the interests of dragonkind, and that an opportunistic attempt to grab power drove my belief in such absurd slander. So infuriated was I that I burst into laughter. After refuting his accusations with a few choice words, and without even finishing my Quenepa Berries, I departed.
He is always like this. He scorns his kin, mocks his bloodline, and never shares his thoughts with other dragons, yet he resents them for failing to understand him. But if he refuses to speak his mind, how could anyone ever fathom what he truly intends?
Our Sovereign's indulgence toward him knows no bounds, so much so that he can no longer distinguish right from wrong. Whether his actions were just or misguided, the Sovereign would always respond with gentle agreement. And precisely because of this, his unease only grows deeper. No matter which path he takes, he is always met with the same tender light, leaving him utterly lost as to which road he truly walks. In the end, his suspicions toward his kin are nothing but reflections of his self-doubt.
I pity him.
...

The consequences of the phlogiston theft worsen by the day. Most of the other rulers allow humans to use phlogiston to kill and conquer each other, some even encouraging them to commit more atrocities. They seem to see this as an effective means of controlling the human population... or perhaps they derive mere amusement from it.
The flood of refugees surging northward grows ever larger, and the tidings they bring grow ever more horrifying. The chieftain of Kacho'pinik offered his daughter in marriage to the leader of the Culhua, hoping to win their allegiance. Yet the Culhua instead cut out her (...), sacrificed her to (...), and marched (...) upon their villages, for their food stores were more abundant. They do not understand how we extract vitality from blood, yet they ape our ways nonetheless, offering up meaningless slaughter to their imagined gods.
I spoke with Kemonel. Even she felt a pang of reluctance, though her pity was not for humans, but for her own kin, now reduced to mere beasts. More and more humans have begun taming vishaps, turning them into tools of slaughter, for even stripped of their intellect, their claws and fangs still rend flesh with ease. Thus, Kemonel has sought to ally with those humans who yearned for peace, hoping to harness their souls to weave an eternal, blissful dream-realm for the dragons of her domain. Even the unfortunate fallen might shed the forms that imprison them and find happiness and solace within this dream.
It is not an unfeasible plan, but her approach would inevitably weaken oversight of human settlements, inviting greater suffering upon these frail creatures who have come from beyond the skies.
The sorrow of humankind stems from their lack of hierarchy. Dragons are born to submit to their superiors and command their inferiors. Even if I appeared before them in human guise, they would instantly catch my scent, recognize my station, and obey my orders — for it is the law carved into their blood, their path ordained by nature, for the weak to revere the strong, offspring to follow their sire, and subjects to serve their sovereign. But humans are different. Humans are born to deceive their betters, torment weaker kin, and even betray entire clans — or slaughter the very blood that gave them life — for nothing but selfish gain. Their eyes reflect no path that belongs to them, or if they did, they shall doubtless invent endless excuses to forsake said path. Without proper guidance and restraint, they repeat the same atrocities, never learning from their past misdeeds.
All defilement of life is blasphemy, an unforgivable stain upon our Sovereign's honor. Thus, only by elevating humans to stand on equal footing with dragons, forcing them to learn the necessity of the weak kneeling to the strong, and the meaning of their ordained path, can their capacity for violence be utterly purged.
...It is an idea that has yet to come to pass. If the reaver from beyond the sky can seal off an entire planet to force humanity into their imposed order, then why might I not seal off my domain in turn? Let it become an impervious refuge. Let nothing within depart, and nothing without enter. A closed, ordered system, where life's future may be sculpted without flaw...
Let this plan be named "Xibalba," a title borrowed from the humans of my domain, their primitive myths whispering of an underworld. Should it succeed, neither the sovereign rulers nor the Abyssal foe shall be able to breach its sealed laws. A fitting title for an incorruptible sanctuary...
...
The king's waking days grow rarer, and so too do our chances to commune with him. He approved Kemonel's plan, as well as my own.
Like Kukulkan, I grow perplexed... What path may bring true joy to our Sovereign? What kind of path may allow this land to prosper for ten thousand years to come?
I do not know. The Xibalba project is progressing smoothly, but even if it were progressing perfectly, I could not convince myself. If the hierarchy of power has failed to ease our Sovereign's suffering... If I cannot, by the wisdom he granted me, fathom how to truly please him... Then by what right do I dare ordain a path for all other lives?
Perhaps... I need to observe the humans more, humans who have yet to be tainted by their laughable traditions. If there truly is still hope, then...

...
After the review, I paid a visit to Je'lal, and asked for her aid in forging a bow as a farewell gift for my daughter.
After telling her why I had sought her out, she remained silent for about two minutes. Her turquoise eyes blazed as she replied:
"You would do well to remember, Eighth Lord, that you are exploiting a kindness I never owed you in the first place. How dare you ask me to debase myself and forge crude weapons for those insignificant humans? Had anyone but the Sovereign or you uttered such insolence, I would have already ripped the blasphemous tongue from their mouth and stitched a new crimson gown for my jades with it. I refuse. I will not entertain this ludicrous insult. I would not deign to reconsider even if you laid a hundred thousand slaves at my feet."
Before I could say anything else, she flew away without looking back. To reject it so vehemently from the start... With her surly temperament, that essentially meant a "yes."
...
As expected, Je'lal secretly sent a Source Servant to deliver the forged bow, and sent also a message that I might not misunderstand her: This bow was "made by a common dragon craftsman in her territory," a "shoddy piece made with worthless scrap," and had "absolutely nothing to do with her."
As she claimed, she truly does not forge any "crude weapons." Those jade pieces were treasured (...) she had hoarded for ages, ones that even (...) might not scorch. A shame about the bowstrings, though, as they remained ordinary. Had I known, I would've had her forge a sword instead.
Well, no matter. My dearest daughter ought to adore this "gift from some common dragon craftsman," Ix Je'lal K'ua'l Ka'. I shall give thought to remuneration later...

imgDesc.text: Living with the Qucusaurs, this is the home of the tribe known as the Flower-Feather Clan. Every day, members of the tribe fly with the Qucusaurs, patrolling their territory from the air.

In order to deal with the crisis brought on by the ash that once enveloped the foothills like fog, the priests of the Masters of the Night-Wind once studied the secret art of how to make graffiti that would be visible even through the mists. It is said that this was the origin of the unique power of the graffiti here.
Walls with graffiti that chronicles the stories of the heroes of the past. But are the stories recorded here true stories that once happened, or the shadows of another story...

customize.text: The Abyss Invasion

Due to damage to the Natlan's Ley Lines and the contamination of the Night Kingdom, the Abyss was not driven out of Natlan during the Cataclysm. For five hundred years, it grew in power by attacking the tribes. At first, the attacks seemed random, and the Abyss appeared to be a natural phenomenon, but it later turned out that the attacks occurred at the tribes' vulnerable points. Using memories stored in Natlan's Night Kingdom, the Abyss studied all the tribes' weaknesses, as if possessing a consciousness. And five hundred years after the Cataclysm, it launched a full-scale invasion of all the tribes of Natlan simultaneously. The Fatui, under the command of Capitano, formed an alliance with the Pyro Archon and joined forces to combat the Abyss.

The Pyro Archon Mavuika had already witnessed a battle of similar magnitude five hundred years ago, during the Cataclysm. Although the Natlanese at that time had managed to drive the Abyss into the depths of the Night Kingdom, they knew it would eventually erupt again. Their calculations estimated that they would have a maximum of five hundred years before the Night Kingdom was completely lost to the Abyss, but as it was, Natlan lay in ruins, and the civilization was dying. It was necessary to unite the tribes, otherwise, it would be impossible to dream of a final victory. So, the Archon had a long and involved discussion with the heroes of each tribe and finally came up with a five-hundred-year-long plan to save Natlan. During this time, the Archons and chiefs were to rebuild the tribes, and when the time came, the Wayob would again choose six heroes of Natlan with the Ancient Names of Xbalanque's companions. Mavuika entered the Sacred Flame to be reborn five hundred years later.

Five hundred years later, when Mavuika's plan needed only one hero recognized by their Ancient Name, the Abyss attacked across Natlan. With the Pyro Archon deprived of the power of the Sacred Flame to counterattack, this was the Abyss's best opportunity. Despite the Flower-Feather Clan's warriors' resistance, Quahuacan Cliff was soon tainted by the Abyss. When the Traveler and Paimon were about to go to the aid of the Flower-Feather Clan, they encountered the tribe's peacekeeper, Chasca, and her sister, the doctor, Chuychu, surrounded by monsters near the Stadium of the Sacred Flame. Although the attack was repelled, Chuychu was gravely wounded. Even when the Traveler cleansed her body of the Abyss, it was too late. The loss of her sister awakened the Abyssal energy within Chasca, dormant since her childhood injury, but she was able to bend it to her will. The pain Chasca felt at the loss of Chuychu awakened her Ancient Name, and her ancestor, Menilek, who bore the same Ancient Name five hundred years ago, recognized her as the sixth and final hero of Natlan.

Returning with Chuychu to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame, Chasca asked for care for her sister's body and went to the Pyro Archon to fulfill Chuychu's hopes and sacrifice. Once all six heroes necessary for Mavuika's plan had been recognized by their Ancient Names, she used their power and the divine throne to banish the Abyss. This power helped destroy the previously invulnerable Abyss Tumors, and the Ode of Resurrection allowed the resurrection of all Natlanese who had perished after using this power. Mavuika was able to attack Gosoythoth, forcing it to flee into the Night Kingdom.

But even after the war with the Abyss was over, many could not recover from the event. The Traveler, Paimon, and one of the six heroes of Natlan, Iansan of the Collective of Plenty, aided in the Flower-Feather Clan reconstruction. When they arrived at the settlement, they found out that some warriors of the tribe were struck by sudden and powerful Abyssal energy, damaging not only their bodies but also their minds. This mental suffering was linked to repressed fears and anxieties. One of the warriors, Atoco, believed he was in cold water while the Abyss was catching up with him, calling for his Saurian companion, who had died four years earlier during an Abyss attack. To help the victim, Iansan lit a fire for him, and the Traveler indwelled in a Qucusaurus resembling the warrior's companion. Realizing it wasn't his companion, the warrior awoke from his hallucinations.

Another victim, Cochitta, was about twelve years old when her parents were killed by Abyss monsters before her eyes, leaving her and her younger brother alone. Afterward, Cochitta trained diligently, but was too weak to fight. Until one day, the monsters burst into her and her brother's home. When guards arrived, they found Cochitta standing with a weapon in her trembling hands, her brother hiding behind her. The defeated monster lay at her feet, but she didn't even look at it, and just kept repeating the same thing over and over — <color=#ffffffd9>"you're the only family I have left. I won't let anything happen to you."</color> And from then on, she changed dramatically. She began participating in all the battles against the Abyss and gradually earned a reputation as a brave warrior. Everyone in the tribe thought she had finally overcome her fear, but Cochitta had only buried it deeper, and a powerful blast of Abyssal energy unleashed it once again. To help the warrior, Iansan and the Traveler went with her to fight the Abyssal monsters, and she awoke from her hallucinations, realizing the Abyss wasn't so terrifying.

The third victim, the warrior Ocotlan, believed the tribesmen around him were monsters of the Abyss, and even saw his father as nothing more than a monster. Ocotlan was a brave and determined warrior, ready to fight to the last, and so he could not be shaken from his hallucinations. The warrior was aided by the Fatui Harbinger Capitano, who had witnessed similar symptoms during the Cataclysm 500 years earlier. People experienced emotional instability, lack of energy, or mental deterioration. This disease, known as the Abyssal Corrosion Syndrome, could cause hallucinations or mental breakdowns, making those infected extremely dangerous to themselves and those around them. A military physician from Khaenri'ah, Guthred, created a cure called the Draught of Lucidity, a kind of medicine that can dispel the psychological impact of the Abyss. To speed up the development of the cure, Guthred experimented on himself and died shortly after inventing the elixir. The treatment had serious side effects, such as lifelong migraines, so it was only used in the most extreme cases. The Traveler and Iansan fought with Ocotlan in order to force him to take the medicine during the battle. Thanks to the elixir, Ocotlan awoke from his hallucinations and was able to recognize his father.

customize.text: Phlogiston Wings

When warriors of the Flower-Feather Clan fail the flying trials to join the elite flying squad and gain the approval of the Qucusaurs for a long time, they become "wingless." Some wingless accept their fate and find a new calling, while others spend their entire lives trying to return to the sky. During a battle with the Abyss several decades ago, the tribe's elder and captain of the flying squad, Allpa, was wounded. Afterward, she was unable to return to the sky and began wandering Natlan. During this time, she gave birth to a child, Tepal, who gave her new hope. She wanted to be a mother who soared the skies day and night, not a wingless wanderer. But his father wanted to settle down and give the child a safe life in the tribe, so their feelings gradually faded. Tepal's father started a new family in the Children of Echoes tribe and took Tepal for himself, and Allpa returned to the Flower-Feather Clan alone.

The elder hadn't seen her son for many years, but one day he appeared on her doorstep, eager to take the flying test. But when the Qucusaurs rejected him, Allpa felt hurt and angry. Together, they created "phlogiston wings," a flying machine worn on the back. It can be operated using a hand-held trackball, which in turn controls the flow of gaseous phlogiston. Using mechanisms from Ochkanatlan, Tepal built a massive flying laboratory hidden in the clouds. During research, it was discovered that wild Qucusaurs, who possessed the natural ability to process gaseous phlogiston, could be used to create the hand-held trackballs. Tepal didn't want to use the Saurians, but during one of the experiments, unstable gaseous phlogiston exploded, killing a man.

Allpa, wanting to fulfill her son's dream of a sky accessible to all, abandoned all experiments and began using the Qucusaurs. One of the kidnapped Saurians was the tribal heroine Chasca's niece, Chime. When her mother, Coya, began attacking people, wanting her daughter back, Allpa ordered her capture as well. Coya's attack played into the elder's hands, as it allowed her to demonstrate the danger of the Qucusaurs and convince other tribe members to abandon their interactions with them. Furthermore, she allowed the use of phlogiston wings in flying tests, so that even those who had become wingless could join the squad. Allpa believed that this was the only way the tribe could develop further, and was even prepared to seize the tribe and kill the chieftain and other elders.

After the Traveler, Paimon, and Chasca's intervention, Allpa was stopped, and all the Qucusaurs in the lab were saved. During a confrontation with the elder, the unstable mechanism from Ochkanatlan was about to explode, but was transported away from the tribe in time, saving the clan's settlement from the lab's fall. Many tribe members sided with Mutota and the Qucusaurs, so the rebellion within the Flower-Feather Clan failed. The sky lab was dismantled and converted into a sky prison, where Allpa and her supporters were imprisoned.

customize.desc:
A Saurian with large, supple wings that can glide through the air for long periods.
It is said that the ancestors of the Qucusaurs were the closest in form to the mighty winged dragons, and that they could soar through the sky like clouds. According to the storytellers, when the greatest of such dragons spread its wings, the entire sky would be blotted out. Of course, the Qucusaurs we see today no longer possess such forms, but the claws they hide within their downy feather coats remain as sharp as ever.

A young Qucusaur with a light, agile body.
Its neck and wings have yet to fully develop, and it still has a long way to go before it can wield gaseous phlogiston. There are stories of older Qucusaurs pushing younglings off cliffs to encourage them to fly. While the truth of such tales is uncertain, as long as it keeps practicing day and night, there can be no doubt that the soft-feathered fledgling will eventually grow strong and resilient.

customize.text: Pakpaka Flying School

One day, at the Pakpaka Flying School training grounds, the Traveler, Paimon, and their Tepetlisaurus companion, Little One, met a boy named Taruka and his Qucusaurus companion, Oberon. The boy believed that the school's trainer, Lamizana, was acting suspiciously and secretively. Furthermore, he constantly tried to communicate with Taruka's sister. Although Lamizana was supposed to be organizing the air races, he delegated this responsibility to his assistant, Paran. Taruka also overheard a conversation in which Lamizana and a second man discussed payment for something. He asked the Traveler and Paimon to follow the trainer, and although they were skeptical of the seriousness of the situation, they agreed. Heading west of the cliff, they discovered a camp guarded by Iktomisaurs and tribal warriors. Infiltrating the camp, they overheard a conversation about some goods that needed to be delivered to the air race. As Paimon, Little One, and the Traveler, who indwelled in an Iktomisaurus, were about to leave, they were discovered by a woman named Quilla, who called to the Iktomisaurus to follow her. Someone spilled a box of Saurus Crackers outside, and the Traveler and Little One took advantage of the opportunity to escape. When they returned to Taruka to tell her what they had seen, Paran approached them with his white dog and asked them to participate in the race, as another participant had declined. The Traveler agreed, and Paimon thought his voice sounded familiar.

When the day of the air race arrived, the Traveler won, but Taruka and Oberon were missing from the finish line, so Paimon and the Traveler set out to find them. During their search, they encountered Lamizana, who was suddenly attacked by Iktomisaurs. After the Traveler helped repel the attack, he revealed that Oberon and Taruka had been kidnapped. It turned out that Lamizana planned to rig the race so that he and Taruka would compete on a different course but with the same finish line, in order to finish early. When Taruka's sister finished, she would witness the boy being attacked by young Saurians. At that moment, Lamizana would arrive and rescue Taruka, earning the boy's sister's approval. But the plan got out of hand, and the Saurians, gorging on the Saurus Crackers they were selling, not only attacked Taruka but kidnapped him. Quilla accused "a blond person and their white pet," whose description matched both the Traveler and Paimon, as well as Paran and his dog, of the kidnapping. To prove their innocence, the Traveler, Little One, and Paimon escaped to search for Taruka.

After indwelling in an Iktomusaurus again, the Traveler smelled a delicious aroma and discovered a Saurus Cracker with a letter implicating Quilla in selling the strange crackers. When they infiltrated the camp, Taruka fled, leaving Oberon, who had gorged himself on Saurus Crackers. Taking the Qucusaurus with them, the Traveler, Little One, and Paimon prepared to leave the camp, but were stopped by Quilla and her Iktomisaurus. During the Saurian battle, Little One and Oberon defeated the Iktomisaurus, and Quilla escaped. By the time they returned to the flight school, Taruka had returned and revealed the truth about what had happened.

customize.text: Legend of Kuntur

According to legend, long, long ago, a bright star, where Qoyllor lived, shone in the sky. Her father, the Sun, bestowed upon her power, which he commanded her to cherish. Just as people on the ground gaze up in awe at the starry sky, she often looked down upon the life of the tribes in Natlan. One day, she leaned too far forward and accidentally fell from the sky. Falling to the ground, the star lost its former brilliance, and her power shattered into fragments that were scattered across the land. Without it, Qoyllor could no longer return to the sky. For a long time, Qoyllor wandered Natlan in search of the fragments of her star, facing many dangers, but all her searches were in vain. One day, by utter chance, she encountered the fierce warrior and hunter, Ukuku. Upon learning of her plight, he agreed to help her search for the scattered shards of her star so she could return. Together, they set off on their roamings: they climbed high mountains and ventured into deep ravines, overcoming hordes of enemies and making scores of friends. Gradually, Qoyllor adapted to life on the ground and became a true Natlanese.

After years of fruitless searching, Qoyllor decided that, in the same way that she had become a part of the tribe, her lost power had long since been found. She asked Ukuku if he had grown tired of chasing such an elusive goal, but the only answer he gave was a short <color=#ffffffd9>"Sorry."</color> She didn't understand why the hunter was apologizing, as he had always been kind to her, and from the very beginning of their search, they had found no clue about the lost power. Qoyllor and Ukuku were to form a family together, settling down in a corner of the tribe, and had a child named Kuntur. Ukuku's cunning neighbor, from time to time, began speaking badly of Ukuku in front of Qoyllor, embellishing his stories with malicious barbs. At first, Qoyllor paid no attention to this gossip, but over time, doubts began to creep into her heart. She didn't want to make a big deal out of nothing, so she tried to uncover the truth through playful remarks. Under the pressure of her questioning, Ukuku soon confessed that, in fact, he long ago found some star shards. But by that time, Ukuku had already developed feelings for her, so he decided not to give up the shards, to keep her on the ground. After hearing Ukuku's confession, Qoyllor felt sadness and anger. Realizing she could never forgive Ukuku, Qoyllor demanded the star shards back, but he refused. Ignoring his pleas, Qoyllor left the tribe she had once considered home with Ukuku's Iktomisaurus companion and set out to wander again. She left a huge work of graffiti on the vast expanse of land so that her Sun-father could see it from the sky. Qoyllor's father heard her plea, quickly bringing her back to the sky. Ukuku's deceit and betrayal angered the Sun, and as punishment, he was blinded by the Sun's golden arrows. From then on, wherever he went, the Sun would retreat behind the clouds, leaving him without a trace of sunlight.
After Qoyllor had returned to the skies, Ukuku, blinded by the sun's golden arrows, remained within the tribe, raising the still-young Kuntur alone. Wherever Kuntur appeared, the sun would retreat behind a thick layer of clouds, depriving the world of its light. Although the people did not banish them from the tribe, they avoided the father and son, fearing the sun's wrath. Kuntur grew up a pale youth with eyes like stars. He longed for an Iktomisaurus companion, but no one wanted to live without sunlight. And although he was unable to find a companion for a long time, he would not tolerate ridicule and responded by fighting. At first, he always lost due to his weakness, but over time, he became stronger and more capable.

One day, an old man in ragged clothing came to the tribe, asking for water. The people took pity on him and invited him into their home, feeding him dinner, but the old man ate for a whole week and was never satiated. So the old man began visiting every house that would feed him, but sooner or later, they would send him away. Only Kuntur's house did not entertain the old man. Seeing how Kuntur chased the old man away, many in the tribe could not help but ridicule him again, but no one guessed that the old man in tattered clothes was the infamous sorcerer Rumi in disguise. He cast an evil spell on the people who had let him in but failed to satisfy his appetites, and led away all the tribe's Saurians. The tribe sent forth their three mightiest warriors to bring the Saurians back, but none of them returned. When the tribe had already given up hope of bringing them back, Kuntur volunteered to go after them.
Rumi knew that Kuntur was hated by the sun, so he summoned up layers of mist to surround the warrior. However, the young man had been trained by his blind father since childhood, and so he could find his way by sound and smell. Rumi then sent three talking Pakpakas, three tribal warriors transformed by an evil sorcerer. They spoke the very deceptions Rumi had snared them with, but Kuntur had hated lies since childhood and could always see through them at a glance. After enduring all the trials, Kuntur finally found Rumi and saw the captured Saurians. The sorcerer tried to frighten the youth, but neither towering waves nor running lava could scare him. Rumi then cast an evil spell on the captured Saurians, then turned into a cloud of smoke and disappeared. Kuntur freed the Iktomisaurs and found the bravest of them. The youth wanted to go after the sorcerer with the Iktomisaurus, but it refused. Realizing that otherwise he would be no different from Rumi, Kuntur released the Saurian and set out alone.

Kuntur tracked the magician Rumi for a long time, battling the animals he could transform into, but he was no closer to his goal. One day, he heard a familiar cry of an Iktomisaurus he had freed. Kuntur had earned his respect, so the Iktomisaurus began to show him the way, and even the wily sorcerer could not escape. Rumi transformed into a capybara and dove into the water, but the Iktomisaurus summoned a cyclone with its wings, and Kuntur, riding the wind, raced after the sorcerer. Shocked, Rumi leapt out of the water, transforming into a bird that immediately made for the skies above, but Kuntur mounted the Iktomisaurus and pursued it, eventually catching up with the sorcerer. Seeing that there was nowhere to run, Rumi turned into a cobblestone, but Kuntur clung to the cobblestone with a death grip: <color=#ffffffd9>"Fly! Higher, my friend, higher!"</color> They soared higher and higher until they reached the highest cloud layer, where Kuntur saw the sun for the first time. But before he could speak, the sun brought forth cloud layers, surrounding them in a thick shroud. Kuntur and his companion had no choice but to navigate through the thunder, rain, and storm. It was so cold up there that even Kuntur's eyelids were swathed in frost, and the rock that Rumi had transformed into was frozen solid.
Having overcome trial after trial, Kuntur and his companion returned to the tribe, and the stone that Rumi had turned into was placed in a suitable location. The three warriors who had been turned into Pakpakas by the sorcerer were themselves restored to human form. They continued to avoid Kuntur out of shame and regret, as they had tried to deceive him. Thus did Kuntur prove himself to his tribe and win glory. But most importantly, he now had an Iktomisaurus companion of his own.

customize.text: Eleventh Lord

Several thousand years ago, the future of Natlan was ruled by the Pyro Sovereign and the thirteen Sovereign Rulers he created using Secret Source technology. They were forms of artificial intelligence whose power surpassed even the most ancient dragons. Two thousand years ago, almost all of them were destroyed during the war with the first Pyro Archon Xbalanque and the first heroes. The Eleventh Sovereign Ruler,
was the proudest of all the Sovereign Rulers and the most hostile toward humanity. She survived the war, but lost her refuge. Her pride in belonging to the dragonkind vanished, and the territory once under her dominion disappeared without hope of return. She was tormented by the question: should she strike back at humanity and take revenge, or should she seek a new home? Unable to find an answer, the Eleventh Lord's mind split into two: one, the Sovereign Ruler, sworn to avenge humanity, and the other, the malfunction, eager to find a new home. These personalities separated completely, acquiring separate physical entities. Mirror of the Dawning Morn sought control of the machines in the Eighth Lord, Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers' territory, located beneath the Quahuacan Cliff, and to do so, she needed to destroy the "malfunction" and acquire its core. She attempted to deceive the Natlan heroines, Ixquieh and Lianca, posing as the other personality and convincing them that the "malfunction" was a threat, but they saw through the deception. Lianca exploited her arrogance and turned her plan against her, using the full power of the territory to imprison her within the Xibalba prison created by the Eighth Lord. Mirror of the Dawning Morn placed a curse on the malfunction so that it could never find a home.
<color=#ffffffd9>"If she truly harbors pro-human sentiment... then for every ounce of goodwill she feels, may her mind be flooded with pain of immeasurable proportions."</color>

The First Speaker of the Flower-Feather Clan, Lianca, did not want the "malfunction" to fall under the influence of the Eleventh Lord and also wanted to protect it from the ruler of the Grand Alliance, Och-Kan, who had become a tyrant and wanted to destroy all descendants of dragons. Lianca had no intention of fighting him, as they owed each other more than their lives, but her clan would never bend the knee to anyone. Ixquieh implanted the Moon Wheel, an ancient artifact through which the Three Moon Goddesses communicated with their followers and which her mother had left to Lianca, into the "malfunction." The First Speaker then sent it on a journey to find a new home. Lianca altered the malfunction's memory settings to erase its memories and protect it from the curse of Mirror of the Dawning Morn. To prevent the Eleventh Lord from escaping Xibalba, the First Speaker strengthened the prison and sealed off her mother's territory.

For two thousand years, Mirror of the Dawning Morn remained a prisoner within the territory of the Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers, gradually seizing control of systems and processes until its influence permeated every inch of this prison. The final step to freeing herself was to destroy the core within the "malfunction." After two millennia of wandering, the malfunction finally found a family when the genius Aino transformed its core into a robot named Ineffa. But the curse of the Eleventh Lord persisted, and Ineffa continued to feel pain, thinking about home. To find her home, she traveled to Natlan, where the Eleventh Lord tricked her into the underground ruins, posing as the Eighth Lord. She explained that Ineffa needed to be rebuilt from scratch using the Secret Source mechanisms located within the Eighth Lord's territory to truly sever the connection between the personalities and break the curse's power. But when Mirror of the Dawning Morn gained control of Ineffa's body and destroyed her core, she was able to break the curse with the Moon Wheel and regain control of her body, defeating the Eleventh Overlord.

Through this process of distorting the past's memories into more abstruse and sordid forms, they gradually draw closer to Irminsul's core, threatening to undermine its very existence.
Some say that these aberrations work constantly to corrupt the many colors of light, leaving only pitch-black information in their stead. Such a hypothesis seems to be confirmed by the branches they extend outward, as if to pierce the void itself...

According to the storytellers, when the greatest of such dragons spread its wings, the entire sky would be blotted out. Of course, the Qucusaurs we see today no longer possess such forms, but the claws they hide within their downy feather coats remain as sharp as ever.

These tribal warriors trust their own two hands more than any weapon. Above all else, they are renowned for their lithe and agile bearing.

Proud sword wielders whose blade strokes are as sweeping as a Qucusaur's outstretched wingspan. Blood sprays forth like scattered feathers from the wounds they inflict.

customize.name: Winged Warrior: Skymaster
customize.desc:
A warrior from the clifftops, and a tribal guardian that patrols the steep mountain ridges.
By observing and emulating the claw strikes of airborne Saurians, these warriors have grasped the essence of harnessing their own power. Their kicks, delivered from up high, should not be underestimated.

customize.name: Qucusaurus Warrior: Blazing Sky
customize.desc:
A powerful warrior from the clifftops, whose bravery has been acknowledged and for which they may wear the Saurian Crown.
Among the many varieties of Saurians, the Qucusaurs stand particularly proud, and this is a trait that is shared by the Qucusaurus Warriors who are able to obtain their recognition. It is said that in the past, tribal warriors would watch these crimson Saurians amuse themselves by tossing flaming stones from great heights; and that it was this that first inspired them to set off projectiles to cause explosive chain reactions. This concept, gradually refined over time, is said to have been the origin of many of the Flower-Feather Clan's firearms.

customize.name: Qucusaurus Warrior: Heartstar Hammer
customize.desc:
A powerful warrior from the clifftops, whose bravery has been acknowledged and for which they may wear the Saurian Crown.
Even in Natlan, the Nation of Pyro, members of the Flower-Feather Clan have a unique approach when it comes to wielding fire and flames. For these tribal warriors, armed as they are with heavy hammers, flames are something that burst forth from violent collisions, symbols of intense passion. When they do battle, the fight usually ends within an instant— and they are always the ones who stand victorious.

customize.name: Burning-Aflame Wayob Manifestation
customize.desc:
The Flower-Feather Clan believe in and worship the Wayob, which manifests upon the land with the power of totems and Nightsouls.
They say that long ago, Wayob Manifestations looked very different from how they do today, taking on a rougher form that was more akin to that of an obsidian statue. But once their outline had been recorded in woven scrolls, there have been few changes in their appearance since.
The people of the Flower-Feather Clan believe their Wayob has the power to control fire and burning flames, and can also control the flow of heat and blazing winds.

customize.text: Wildlife

customize.name: Capybara
customize.desc:
These herbivores, which often dwell close to the water, are famous for their steely, stoic "won't even twitch if lightning strikes right next to their toes" disposition. Tourists consider them to be the paragon of animal friends.
Capybaras like to zone out while having a soak in the water, or sun themselves on the shore, and it's quite common for them to barely move for most of the day, as though not a single thing in the world could possibly perturb their calm demeanor and make them anxious. Despite their fluffy appearance, their hairs are actually quite hard and tough. If you pet them in the same direction as their coat of hair, it feels relatively smooth, but should you pet them in the opposite direction, you may end up with a scratched hand. Perhaps that is the reason even famished predators do not regard these completely harmless and quite defenseless little friends as prey...

customize.name: Cacaua Goat
customize.desc:
These gentle beasts can be found all over Teyvat and were among the earliest to be domesticated by humans.
Contrary to what the name might suggest, Cacaua Goats do not give off a uniquely bitter odor. This unforgettable name originates from the hue of their wool, which closely resembles that of food and drink made from Cacahuatl. For traditional Natlan dyers, achieving a chocolate or xocoatl color is not an easy task, as the slightest mistake might result in a dirty-looking finish like rain-soaked mud. The wool of these robustly-built Cacaua Goats has a smooth texture and a clean, chocolatey tone, which is why they are so highly valued...

customize.text: Map
Location Map
"Flower-Feather Clan"
Flower-Feather Clan's Settlement

At the top of the Quahuacan Cliff, where strong mountain winds blow, lies the settlement of the Flower-Feather Clan. Almost the entire tribe is built on a complex network of platforms, ladders, and walkways to accommodate the unique demands of the terrain. The tribe uses very lightweight wooden ladders and installs hot air balloons beneath the platforms to reduce maintenance costs. If balloons are seen as the wings that lift the Flower-Feather Clan into the skies, then these wooden platforms might be considered the "giant claws" that anchor the tribe to the mountains. As one of the proudest tribes in Natlan, the members of the Flower-Feather Clan tend to compete fiercely in various contests to showcase their excellence, and the tribe has certain restrictions on house decoration and renovation. In such unique environments as the Quahuacan Cliff, excessive modifications and decorations can pose a threat to the safety of both the buildings and the entire platform, with potentially disastrous consequences. Therefore, the Flower-Feather Clan restricts decorations to those that do not alter the structural integrity or form of the buildings. There are plenty of cliffside murals near the Flower-Feather Clan, but not many flat, open areas large enough for a giant work of land art.

The settlement's main landmark is the Flower-Feather Clan's Obsidian Totem Pole, a legendary artifact said to "be linked to the tribe's Wayob, and can listen to the wishes of the people." People believe that as long as the pole stands, the tribe continues to soar. Currently, this Obsidian Totem Pole is under the care of Abundi, from whom people can accept monster bounties, supply orders, and other relevant tasks to elevate their reputation within the Flower-Feather Clan.

The tribe's second most important location is the flight trial grounds, where the fate of many flying squad members and squad candidates is decided. When the tribe was responsible for patrolling and defending all of Natlan, the flying squad was the best of the best — the fiercest warriors in the nation. Anyone wishing to become a rider must train tirelessly and then earn the approval of the Qucusaurs. To join the elite squad, a special flying test is held, during which candidates must demonstrate mastery of the relevant skills and earn the favor of the Qucusaurs. Until recently, the flying squad captain was Elder Allpa, now imprisoned in a sky prison, and the current tribe chief, Mutota, was once an ace pilot. Mutota doesn't try to be a strict leader, but the Flower-Feather Clan has certain rules of conduct and caution when interacting with the most arrogant Saurians in Natlan.

Only a few are selected for the elite flying squad, and sometimes, after several failed attempts to pass the flying test and gain the Qucusaurs's approval, they become so disillusioned that they abandon their dream of the sky. They decide to give up trying forever, and within the clan, such individuals are known as "wingless." Some wingless continue to dream of flight and spend their days looking at the Cinder City, while others resign themselves to their fate and find new pursuits. Two wingless ones organized the "Target Balloon" and "Eyes on the Feathered Prize" challenges, where anyone, even without a flying license, can participate and earn rewards.

The Flower-Feather Clan settlement houses the clinic of Natlan's best Sauro-Vet, Ifa. It can be found by a colorful sign painted by Ifa's best friend, Ororon. Along with his assistant, Cacucu, Ifa sees patients from all over Natlan. Besides the clinic, the settlement also features two certified Genius Invokation TCG players, Utsil and Mukki. Utsil is the tribe's guardian and collects all the Saurian cards and the Saurian blessing. His mentor, Akat from Frida's Palette, drew him a deck of Saurian cards. Mukki is a member of the flying squad and crafts Saurian whistles, instruments used to aid in communication between Saurians and humans.

While traveling along the Quahuacan Cliff, the Traveler, Paimon, and their Saurian companion, Little One, encountered a strange, childlike man south of the Flower-Feather Clan settlement. He introduced himself as a former Marechausse Phantom detective from Fontaine named Magnifico de la Magnificans. After retiring, Magnifico decided to become a photographer and capture the life force in people and objects, and so he came to Natlan, the land of the most shocking elemental lifeforms. When he first met the Traveler and Paimon, he had been without water for several days and was exhausted from thirst, so they saved his life by giving him a drink. Their second encounter took place in the settlement of the Masters of the Night-Wind, where he asked for photographs of an Iktomisaurus from a specific angle and with the right lighting. Their third encounter occurred south of the cliff, where Magnifico wanted to photograph a Qucusaurus diving toward the surface of the waterfall. Although he hid food that might attract the Qucusaurs in the pool below the waterfall, the Saurians never flew at the angle he wanted. Thanks to the help of the Traveler, who had indwelled in a Qucusaurus, the former detective was able to take the most captivating shot. The final photograph Magnifico wanted was of the Tepetlisaurs northwest of the Flower-Feather Clan settlement. As they were framing the shot, the Tepetlisaurus companion of the Traveler and Paimon suddenly noticed something. Following him, the Traveler saw a Sumpter Beast in a cage and the hunters who had captured it. When the little Sumpter Beast was rescued and befriended Little One, Magnifico chose a shot of their interaction for his photograph. Since it was dangerous for the animal to walk alone, and the photographer needed to carry some things, Magnifico took the Sumpter Beast with him.

East of the Flower-Feather Clan, the Traveler, Paimon, and Little One encountered a woman and a Qucusaurus attacking her. The Traveler rushed to her aid and drove off the Saurian, but it turned out to be attacking for medical treatment. The woman, who introduced herself as Mazkal, a Sauro-Vet, asked Little One to give the Qucusaurus some medicine, as it was unwilling to accept treatment from a human. She prepared two types of medicine to choose from: one more beneficial but not very tasty, and the other, pleasant-tasting but less effective. Thanks to Little One's help, the Saurian received treatment, and the Traveler and Paimon returned it to Mazkal.

North of the encounter with Mazkal, an Obsidian Totem leading to the Night Kingdom can be found. There, the soul of Ironbeard, a powerful warrior from the clifftops, whose bravery has been acknowledged and for which they may wear the Saurian Crown, can be dueled. For these tribal warriors, armed as they are with heavy hammers, flames are something that burst forth from violent collisions, symbols of intense passion. When they do battle, the fight usually ends within an instant, and they are always the ones who stand victorious.

While exploring the southern part of Quahuacan Cliff, the Traveler and Paimon discovered a young man named Acomitl locked in a cellar and surrounded by smugglers. Although the Traveler came to his aid and defeated the smugglers, Acomitl refused to leave the cellar. After finding out from nearby Qucusaurs how to get to the young man, the Traveler discovered that he had locked himself in the basement. He had recently passed his riding exam and become a full member of the flying squad. While in reserve, he dreamed of becoming a full member of the flying squad and trained tirelessly to be as good as the others. After days and nights of constant training, the fear of making the slightest mistake, and constant doubts, Acomitl couldn't talk to his parents and sister, his appetite and sleep had vanished, and his character had deteriorated. And when he finally became a full member of the squad, he had to constantly chase the commander, like a firefly, rising up into the sky for the very first time, being told that it had to catch up with a sparrow, and then once it did, that its next target was a shooting star. So he decided to vent his anger by telling the Saurian traders to take all the Qucusaurs, not thinking they would actually do that. He hid in the basement and found himself trapped, and when the Traveler rescued him, he asked him to come up with a good reason to quit the flying squad, as he lacked the courage to do so. To help the young man, the Traveler took part in the trials at the training ground built for Acomitl by his relatives and broke his record. But even despite the broken record, the squad leader refused to let the young man go. After meeting with his father, a flight trainer, and his sister and brother, Acomitl finally decided to quit the squad on his own, and his family supported him.

customize.text: Cliff Coast

On the beach where Traveler and Paimon freed the Sumpter Beast from its cage, there was an incomplete graffiti. To complete it, nine Monetoos should be found. Three of them can be found after playing the game "Bing Bong Ding Dong." Participants sit on the Saurian statue's back to make it move forward. If they don't dismount before the Bing Bong Monetoo counts down to a "ding!", they lose, and the first one to run to the Bing Bong Monetoo wins. Three other Monetoos can be obtained after playing tic-tac-toe with them in the sand using the Iktomisaurus's abilities. The last three Monetoo can be retrieved after playing a game with them and placing a red object into the jar.

Along the coast, near the cliff, the Masters of the Night-Winds' trainee priestess, Conulaf, can be encountered in three different locations. Her training was nearing completion, so, according to her, the tribe's elders told her that ancestral treasures were scattered throughout Natlan: <color=#ffffffd9>"Go do some treasure-hunting, Conulaf!"</color> Under the guise of training, they escorted Conulaf out of the tribe, and she set out to find them. One time, she heard that if she followed an animal's trail, she would find treasure. She followed a Sumpter Beast to camp, but the people mistook her for a thief and locked her in a cart. Another time, the tribe's elders told her that her ancestor, Sanhaj, often bet against people from other tribes and cheated them: <color=#ffffffd9>"Go make and win some bets! That's the only way to qualify as a true Master of the Night-Wind!"</color> Conulaf saw a Saurian competition and bet on an Iktomisaurus, but it lost, and she was locked in a cage. The elders offered her a third trip to see the world, but she was captured and locked away by hilichurls.

At the northern end of the Quahuacan Cliff beach is a dock serving ships to Nod-Krai. This dock was built under the direction of the Pyro Archon after an incident involving a former Fatui agent, Zhuoxin, who had once worked for the Fatui Harbinger Sandrone. He was forced to lead a robot named Ineffa to the ruins of the ancient dragons located beneath the cliff. These ruins once belonged to the foster mother of the Flower-Feather Clan's founder and a Dragonlord, Priestess of Floral Candles and Skyborne Feathers. Within Ineffa was the core of another Sovereign Ruler, the Eleventh Lord Mirror of the Dawning Morn, a part of whose consciousness was imprisoned in the Eighth Lord's territories. It was this core that Sandrone desired. After the Fatui were eliminated, Zhuoxin, along with his wife and daughter, remained in Natlan to help fellow Nod-Krai refugees like himself.

North of the Quahuacan Cliff lies a small island where the Qucusaurus family of the Flower-Feather Clan heroine, Chasca, lived. When Chasca was abandoned by her parents, the Qucusaurus Chimpu became her mother, and Coya became her older sister. Although the girl lacked a beak and claws, she initially considered herself a Saurian. When Chasca began living with humans, Coya suggested that she leave them and come live with her. Chasca could neither agree nor refuse, and her sister viewed this as a betrayal and did not communicate with Chasca for a long time.

In the westernmost part of the area is an Obsidian Totem challenge in the Night Kingdom, where warriors can fight a Wayob Manifestation, "Tupayo's Aid." The Flower-Feather Clan believes in and worships the Wayob, which manifests upon the land with the power of totems and Nightsouls. They say that long ago, Wayob Manifestations looked very different from how they do today, taking on a rougher form that was more akin to that of an obsidian statue. But once their outline had been recorded in woven scrolls, there have been few changes in their appearance since. The people of the Flower-Feather Clan believe their Wayob has the power to control fire and burning flames, and can also control the flow of heat and blazing winds.

customize.text: Malinalco Grotto

Malinalco Grotto lies beneath the Quahuacan Cliff. In the cave's left branch lies the Tenebrous Papilla, a plant-like, parasitic Abyssal monstrosity that has descended from a deep, dark, unfathomable, contorted otherworld. These twisted monstrosities are capable of harnessing the Abyssal powers and infiltrating deep down into the bowels of the earth, extracting memories to imitate and manipulate. Through this process of distorting the past's memories into more abstruse and sordid forms, they gradually draw closer to Irminsul's core, threatening to undermine its very existence. If left unchecked, they will continue Teyvat's decay, perhaps finding a way to twist and reshape even the most ancient memories. Such a hypothesis seems to be confirmed by the branches they extend outward, as if to pierce the void itself.

In the right branch of the grotto grow fruits from which the ancestors of the Masters of the Night-Wind have long produced dyes for woven scrolls. They chose the cave as a location for the graffiti, but did not want to show the unfinished work, so they sealed the cave. And even when the work was completed, the seal was not removed. Since the Malinalco Grotto was closed, the only person who could enter was the great shaman Huitzilin two hundred years ago. To open the cave, one must have the perception of a special color, which is actually the color of memory. The graffiti in the cave depicts the story of the hero Kuntur, who pursued the evil sorcerer Rumi. After coloring the fruits in the graffiti the right colors, the wall will open, revealing a passageway ending in a scene of Kuntur chasing the sorcerer. In the story, the tribe's warriors fell under Rumi's influence and stood in the hero's way, and only by defeating them can one proceed further. Using the Iktomisaurus's powers, images of warriors can be summoned, and defeating them opens a passage to the lower part of the grotto. Using the magical powers of the Monetoo and graffiti, Kuntur can be aided to catch the evil sorcerer.
